Answer: B
Reason: The chest radiograph demonstrates unilateral hyperlucency of the right hemithorax with diminished vascular markings (vessel paucity) and a smaller right hilum, which are classic features of Swyer–James–MacLeod syndrome (post-infectious bronchiolitis obliterans). This condition is strongly associated with a history of recurrent lung infections in childhood and can be accompanied by bronchiectasis.
